Naive: run user code on the API servers. It is a security hole, and slow code blocks everything.

items: Run every submission in an isolated sandbox (Firecracker/gVisor): read-only filesystem, no network, seccomp, strict CPU/memory/time limits.
Decouple with a queue: the API records QUEUED and returns immediately; autoscaled workers run tests and write results; the client polls status every second (the long-running-task pattern).
Contest leaderboard in a Redis sorted set; the score encodes points and time penalty.
Security layers?
MicroVM or gVisor, no network, read-only FS, seccomp filters, resource limits, kill on timeout.
Contest spike?
The queue absorbs it; scale workers on queue depth; pre-warm containers per language.
Polling vs push?
Polling every 1s is simple and fine at this scale; SSE is optional.
Leaderboard ties?
score = points × 1e6 − penalty_seconds.
Executing user code with network access or on shared API hosts.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
Ignoring retries, timeouts and crashes.
